# Close Recap, Tue Nov 10, 2026 (pulled ~4:20 PM ET)

**Hot CPI, then a bear flag.** Core CPI printed **+0.3%** (consensus +0.2%), the number Waller had said could justify a 50 bp hike. The session went gap down, bounced into the old pre-market lows by 10:00, got rejected there, and slid to lows at **12:41**. After that it ground back up into the close. **SPY −0.37%, QQQ −0.68%, IWM −0.69%.** The 10-year hit **5.02%** at its auction, and **NVDA fell −5.5%** on the Huang probe headlines. VIX still closed *lower* at **19.54**.

Sources: the Quant Data API on the user's account (ETF prices, GEX by strike, dark pool, 9k+ unconsolidated flow), Yahoo Finance (futures, indexes, VIX, yields, DXY, oil, gold, stocks, 15-min bars), the Financial Juice RSS feed, X (FirstSquawk, DeItaone, Team2Trading), and Earnings Whispers / ATLAS / Investrade for earnings and the calendar. The browser My Pages weren't touched, so the 'contract flow' Session Date wasn't changed.

Notes on the table:
- ETF highs and lows come from Quant Data 1-minute bars.
- Futures are Yahoo 1-minute data at 15:59. The % change is vs Monday's settle, and the highs and lows are RTH only.
- Overnight highs were ES 7598.75 / NQ 28109 / RTY 2860.7, so the full-day range was much wider.
- Cash indexes: S&P 500 7520.93 (−0.38%), Nasdaq Composite 25066 (−0.74%), NDX 27741 (−0.60%), Dow 52232 (−0.30%), Russell 2000 2821 (−0.68%).

**Cross-asset:**
- VIX **19.54** (−1.9%). Its RTH high was 21.43 at 9:32 and it ground down to 19.29 at 15:52. The equity drop came without fear.
- 10-year **4.98%**, up about 12 bp, with an intraday high of 5.02%. 3-month bill 4.115%.
- DXY **102.27** (+0.6%).
- WTI settled **$86.04 (−0.9%)** and Brent **$91.49 (−1.2%)** (Financial Juice).
- Gold **4038.7 (−1.8%)**.

**Movers:**
- **NVDA −5.5%** (168.89). It was −7.06% at its 15:04 session low (DeItaone).
- MSFT −2.2%, INTC −2.1%, ORCL −1.5%, MU −1.1%, SMH −0.8%, AAPL −0.6%, GOOGL −0.3%.
- Green: **AVGO +3.9%**, AMZN +1.5%, AMD +1.3%, TSLA +0.5%, META flat.
- Last night's earnings: **TTWO +8.3%**, **RKLB +6.5%** (reversing a −7.6% pre-market), ONON −7.5%, SE −1.5%, TDG +0.5%.

## Morning levels: held or broke
- **SPY:**
  - CPI broke the 752.15 PML and the 750 put node before the open.
  - The 9:45 bounce reclaimed 750 (the 9:45 15-min bar closed at 750.74) and tagged **752.14** at 10:08. That's **right at the 752.2 "negate" line and under the 753–754 sign line**. It was **rejected**, and the move never got near the 755–755.4 confluence.
  - The post-data downside target **744 (put node) held to the tick**: the low was 744.86, the **741 PDL was never tested**, and the 735 wall wasn't in play.
  - It closed back at the 750 magnet.
- **QQQ:**
  - The bounce ran straight into the morning's **679.8–681.7 lid** (high 680.95 at 10:01) and **rejected it**. The 681.67 PDH held.
  - It lost the 674 shelf (the 10:30 bar closed at 674.14) and then the **670 put node** (the 11:45 bar closed at 669.85). The low was **667.05**.
  - The 662 PDL never printed. It closed back above the 674 shelf at 674.81.
- **IWM:**
  - The bounce stopped at **281.33**, under the 282.2 old PML.
  - It lost the **280 put node pivot** (the 10:30 bar closed at 278.65). The low of 277.91 was right on the **277 target**, and the **276.84 PDL held**.
  - It closed back on 280.
- **Team2:** Casey posted that he "just traded a bear flag on $QQQ & $IWM today" ([post](https://x.com/Team2Trading/status/2120217536990163236)). That matches the 10:00 rejection and the drop off the lid. After the close he posted a "trifecta trade" breakdown ([post](https://x.com/Team2Trading/status/2120256338039345573)). In a reply he said he's fine trading inside the pre-market range when everything aligns and there's room to the next level.
- **What the morning got right and wrong:**
  - The hawkish CPI scenario and the lids at the old pre-market lows played out.
  - The 744 / 670 / 277 targets were hit, but none of the PDLs were.
  - The history file's whipsaw call (fresh short-dated QQQ puts into the event) fit: the morning flush, the bounce, and the afternoon recovery.

## Drivers
- **Hot CPI → hike repricing.** CPI was +0.4% m/m (forecast +0.3%) and core +0.3% (forecast +0.2%) (Financial Juice, 8:30). At 8:35, traders added bets on a **50 bp December hike**.
  - Northlight's Zaccarelli flagged back-to-back hikes in December and January (DeItaone, 10:21).
  - Deutsche Bank now sees an added 25 bp in January 2027 (Financial Juice, 10:56).
  - FirstSquawk at 16:18: "Wall Street doubled down on wagers that the Fed will need to raise interest rates more aggressively."
- **Bonds.** The 10-year auction **stopped at 5.02%**, vs the 5.010% when-issued (about a 1 bp tail). Bid-to-cover was **2.46** (prior 2.77). The new notes carry a **5% coupon, the highest since 2006** (Financial Juice, 13:02–13:06).
- **Fed speakers:**
  - **Schmid** (13:44–13:50): policy is "fairly accommodative," demand is strong, and inflation is top of mind.
  - **Bowman** (15:30–16:02):
    - "Persistent inflation, firming labor conditions suggest still work to do."
    - Core PCE likely rose 3.3% in October.
    - She wants to see AI and Middle East risks fade before she'd be confident inflation falls next year.
    - She also said financial conditions have tightened and the Fed must weigh the costs of more tightening.
- **NVDA/Huang:**
  - Nvidia hired Wachtell (Joon Kim) to investigate Huang's admitted affair with a Chinese executive accused of espionage (NYT via DeItaone, 14:10).
  - House Republicans are weighing a **subpoena to Huang** and seeking a closed-door briefing (ABC, 14:39–14:58).
  - **Microsoft's market value passed Nvidia's** for the first time since June 2025 (11:50).
  - The stock hit its low at 15:04.
- **AI supply/sentiment:**
  - Anthropic launched office tools that rival Microsoft (12:20) during its IPO roadshow. Its backers are marketing up to $500M of IPO shares (16:00).
  - Nscale may delay its $35B listing "after AI sell-off" (Telegraph, 14:09).
  - The US regulator postponed AI computing futures (FT, 15:00).
- **Iran / Hormuz:**
  - A third tanker exploded in Hormuz (IRIB, 12:09).
  - Iran's Rezai said Hormuz won't reopen until Iran's 7 conditions are met (11:15).
  - Qatar told the G7 it secured "at least two weeks" for diplomacy (13:38).
  - A fire at South Pars was reported under control (14:30).
  - Oil gave back early gains to settle lower.
- **Other:**
  - NY Fed: household debt rose $334B to $19.1T in Q3.
  - BoC minutes kept further hikes open.
  - Jim Jordan was elected House GOP leader (Punchbowl).

**Flip area:** none of the three has a cumulative zero-gamma flip in range. The "flip" lines below are the nearest strike sign changes. All three are **net short gamma and deeper than last night**, and the short gamma is in the *carried* (ex-0DTE) book, so it doesn't expire tonight.

- **SPY** (spot ~750.6):
  - **Net GEX:** **−4.85B** all expirations, **−4.95B ex-0DTE**. That's about 4x last night's −1.18B ex-0DTE, the deepest carried reading of the week so far.
  - **Expiring tonight:** today's 0DTE pin pair, **750P (−3.86B)** and **751C (+4.80B)**.
  - **Put walls (ex-0DTE):** **735 (−0.50B)**, **744 (−0.44B)**, 730 (−0.41B), 740 (−0.35B), 700 (−0.80B).
  - **Call walls:** **770 (+0.51B)**, 780, 790, **800 (+0.65B)**.
  - **Sign changes:** **754**, **757–758**, 760–761.
- **QQQ** (spot ~675.3):
  - **Net GEX:** **−3.07B** all, **−3.43B ex-0DTE** (from −2.63B).
  - **Put walls:** **650 (−0.80B)**, **680 (−0.59B)**, **670 (−0.58B)**, **675 (−0.45B)**, 660 (−0.44B).
  - **Call nodes:** thin and far: 720 (+0.24B), 725, 705, 700.
  - **Sign changes:** **679–680**, 683, 685–686; 659–660 below.
- **IWM** (spot ~280.7):
  - **Net GEX:** **−1.65B** all, **−1.73B ex-0DTE**, nearly double last night's −0.92B.
  - **Puts:** **270 (−0.52B)**, **275 (−0.31B)**, 267, 260.
  - **Calls:** **283 (+0.15B)**, 287, 295, 300 (+0.18B).
  - **Sign changes:** **279–281**, 285–286; 272.5–273 below.
- **Dark pool (today):**
  - **SPY:** a cluster at **748.4–749.9 (~$2.6B combined, biggest 749.85 at $0.86B)** plus **752.74 ($0.76B)**.
  - **QQQ:** **674.76–674.82 (~$1.45B)**, **677.19 ($0.75B)** and **678.88 ($0.71B)**.

## 9,000+ contract prints (Quant Data unconsolidated flow, 165 rows)
Sides: BID 70 / ASK 65 / ABOVE_ASK 15 / MID 11 / BELOW_BID 4. This is a structure read, not Quant Data's labels. **The index ETFs were unusually quiet**: SPY 2 prints, QQQ 2, IWM 10. **There were no new SPY or QQQ put hedges on the hot CPI day.**
- **SPY:** at 14:29, the **Dec 775C 20k was bought back at the ask (closing)** alongside the Dec 800C closing. That unwinds Monday's 775C call overwrite, so the call seller covered.
- **QQQ:** at 13:24, a Dec 680C/715C 10k call spread was closed (680C at the ask, 715C at the bid).
- **IWM:**
  - At 10:57, the **Nov 27 275P was bought above the ask (opening, ~28k total) vs the 267P closing**: puts rolled up again, like Monday's Dec 4 275P roll.
  - At 14:54, **Nov 20 285C 20k was sold and Dec 285C 20k bought** (both opening): an upside calendar rolled out.
  - At 15:43, a Jan 270/240 put spread 10k was closed.
- **NVDA** (41 prints, ~$667M; heavy repositioning on the drop):
  - At 12:14, the **Jan 140P was bought above the ask, 100k opening ($50M), vs the 100P 150k closing**: protection rolled *up*.
  - Also at 12:14, the Feb 165P 75k was closed at the bid ($113M), with the 120P alongside.
  - Calls were **rolled down and in**: Dec 185C 50k bought opening vs Feb 195C closing (11:07); Mar 185C 34.7k bought opening vs Mar 195C closing (11:44); Feb 185C ~50k bought vs Jan 180C closing (13:12).
  - Jun 2027 90P 75k was sold at the bid, opening.
  - Read: holders are adding downside protection *and* rolling calls lower to stay long. That's hedged dip-buying, not capitulation.
- **MSFT:** at 13:05, **Feb 595C 20.4k bought at the ask, opening ($26M)**, plus the Feb 700C, vs the Dec 580C closing. Bullish calls were rolled out.
- **Rates/credit:** HYG 16 prints (mostly puts), LQD 7 (puts opening), TLT 9. The bond selloff showed up in credit hedges.
- **VIX:** Nov 18 25C 28k sold at the bid (9:41) and Dec 21C sold. Call supply came in as VIX faded.
- **Read:** this isn't the snap-back template (no heavy SPY/QQQ put selling at the bid), and it isn't panic either: no fresh index put buying, VIX calls sold, and the SPY overwrite covered. The risk sits in **dealer positioning**: carried short gamma deepened in all three (SPY ~−5B), which per the history file tends to come before larger moves in either direction.

**Takeaway (information, not advice):** a hot core CPI and a 5% 10-year turned yesterday's trend day into a rejection at the old pre-market lows (SPY 752 / QQQ 681 / IWM 281) and a bear flag down to the put nodes (744 / 667 / 278). The PDLs held and the close recovered to mid-range. Dealers now carry **deeper short gamma in all three (SPY ~−5B, QQQ ~−3.4B, IWM ~−1.7B ex-0DTE)** into a bond-holiday session and Friday's PPI, so ranges can widen. The key pivots are **SPY 749–752**, **QQQ 675–681** and **IWM 279–281**.
